root_decision: Retain the scoped subprocess ownership repair, four ownership regressions and strict optional report readers with three regressions. No original-definition, configuration-key, resource-limit or area promotion. The source-transfer cap still fails; JavaScript0.5.2 remains shipping default.
problem: The async contributor-tool runner previously retained a numeric process-group guard after a consuming child wait. That allowed a later group signal after the leader reservation had ended. This is a statically established ordering defect; PID reuse or an unrelated process receiving a signal was not reproduced.
repair: ToolChild owns the Tokio child and group lease. Nonconsuming exit observation precedes final synchronous group cleanup and direct-child fallback. The group lease retires before the first consuming wait, including Drop ordering; Linux ownership loss retires it without an explicit final wait.
Observed leader exit remains separate from both pipe EOFs. Same-group descendant tails are drained under existing time/output/cancellation bounds rather than discarded immediately at leader exit.

Only normal observed exit with both actual EOFs and no stop/read/observation/wait/ownership failure may retain a factual task exit code after solely a final group SIGKILL error. Raw error remains and cleanup_confirmed:false prevents cleanup qualification. Other supervision errors clear the task exit code but retain observed exit facts and factual failure signal; controlled_stop becomes false.

Exceptional signal observations are bounded to three rows, contain only closed target/signal/outcome/kind codes and nullable integer errno, and preserve EPERM as error. ESRCH alone is recorded as absent. Successful signal delivery is not an exhaustive descendant census.

limits_and_remaining_work: Normal ownership assumes a sole consuming reaper. Darwin NOTE_EXIT is not an external-reaper identity check. Linux ECHILD retires the explicit signal lease, but Tokio Drop may still try_wait or orphan-reap; foreign-reaper interoperability is not qualified.
If both group and direct-child SIGKILL fail while the leader remains alive, final wait can outlive the tool budget. This checkpoint does not qualify that exceptional bounded-termination path.
Drop cleanup is nonblocking best effort; eventual Tokio orphan reaping requires a live runtime. No crash-proof, cross-runtime, cross-platform or finite-kernel-wait cleanup guarantee is made.
Direct children must be absent/reaped in regressions; a grandchild may be inactive zombie under a nonreaping PID1. No arbitrary PID reuse or unrelated-process signal was exercised.
Older stdout-only command readers qualify their parsed command results rather than exhaustive process-group cleanup. Strict live readers do not turn shared cleanup failure into relative success.
